messages.subject: issue of implementation of reduceByKey
parts:
Maybe there is a bug in the implementation of reduceByKey. I am not sure.

            reduceVals <- function(part) {
              vals <- new.env()
              keys <- new.env()
              lapply(part,
                     function(item) {
                       hashVal <- as.character(hashCode(item[[1]]))
                       if (exists(hashVal, vals)) {
                         vals[[hashVal]] <- do.call(
                           combineFunc, list(vals[[hashVal]], item[[2]]))
                       } else {
                         vals[[hashVal]] <- item[[2]]
                         keys[[hashVal]] <- item[[1]]
                       }
                     })

The above code piece does not detect hash code collision?

messages.author: f4108b5f63668d70
messages.subject: Re: issue of implementation of reduceByKey
parts:
Hmm -- AFAIK we assume that the hashCode uniquely identifies keys, so we don't need to handle hash collisions. I think this is the case in Scala and Python as well. Do you have a test case that fails that we can look at ?

Thanks
Shivaram

parts:
I don't have such test case. Since an environment is by default backed by a hash table, why not directly index the environment using as.character(key)? Just as the following code piece found in combineByKey:
          function(rdd, createCombiner, mergeValue, mergeCombiners, numPartitions) {
            combineLocally <- function(part) {
              combiners <- new.env()

k <- as.character(item[[1]])
                       if (!exists(k, keys)) {
                         combiners[[k]] <- do.call(createCombiner,
                                                   list(item[[2]]))
                         keys[[k]] <- item[[1]]
                       } else {
                         combiners[[k]] <- do.call(mergeValue,
                                                   list(combiners[[k]],
                                                        item[[2]]))
                       }
                     })
              lapply(ls(keys), function(k) {
                      list(keys[[k]], combiners[[k]])
                     })
